# How to Ask Gemini to Explain Your Bank Statement in Plain English

> **In short:** You can upload a bank statement into Google's Gemini and ask plain-English questions to surface real spending, recurring charges and hidden fees. Gemini can't read your bank account — think of it as a translator for the numbers on your statement.

A monthly bank statement is full of small numbers, merchant codes and fee names that rarely mean anything at first glance. With Google's Gemini, you can hand it that document and ask, in normal sentences, "what am I actually paying for?" — and get a readable answer back. This guide walks you through it, one step at a time.

## Before you start
- A free Google account (the same one you use for Gmail or YouTube).
- Access to Gemini in a browser (gemini.google.com) or the Gemini mobile app — both work for this. The free version is enough for reading a single statement.
- A copy of your monthly bank statement, saved as a PDF or a screenshot — most banks let you download it from their website or app.
- About 10 minutes the first time; once you've done it once, the same questions work on next month's statement.

## Step 1 — Open Gemini and start a fresh chat
Go to **gemini.google.com** in your browser, or open the **Gemini app** on your phone. If you are not signed in, the page will ask you to sign in with your Google account — the same email and password you use for Gmail. Once you are in, look for a button or link along the left side or top of the screen that says something like **"New chat"** or **"Start a new chat"** and click or tap it. A blank conversation opens. If you don't see that exact label, look for a **pencil icon**, a **"+" sign**, or a text box that says **"Ask Gemini"** — any of those will start a fresh conversation.
💬 Example: open the Gemini app, tap "New chat," and you should see an empty text box with the prompt "Ask Gemini" at the bottom.
You'll know it worked when you see an empty text field with no previous messages above it.

## Step 2 — Upload your bank statement
Look for a small **paperclip icon**, a **"+" button**, or an **"Upload"** option near the text box — every version of Gemini has a way to attach a file. Click it, then choose the **PDF** of your statement from your computer or phone. If your statement is a stack of screenshots instead, you can either upload them one at a time or, on the desktop site, drag and drop them all into the chat window together. The file name appears in your message once it uploads. If you can't find an upload option at all, your version may only accept **pasted text** — open your PDF, select all the text (Ctrl+A or Cmd+A), copy it (Ctrl+C or Cmd+C), and paste it (Ctrl+V or Cmd+V) directly into the chat box instead.
💬 Example: "I'm pasting my bank statement below — it's about 3 pages of transactions."
You'll know it worked when a small thumbnail or file name shows up next to your message, and Gemini replies with something like "Got it, I'm reading the statement now."

## Step 3 — Ask for a plain-language summary
Now type a first question in the same chat. Don't ask for anything fancy yet — just ask Gemini to read the statement and tell you, in normal words, what happened in the month. Think of it as asking a friend who is good with numbers to glance at the page and explain it. Be specific about the period, and tell Gemini how you'd like the answer — short bullets, full sentences, whatever you prefer. If Gemini answers with generic budgeting advice instead of reading your actual statement, it probably didn't see the file — re-upload it or paste the text directly into the chat.
💬 Example: "Please read the statement I just uploaded and give me a plain-English summary of what happened in November. List the top 3 things I spent money on and any fees I was charged. Keep it under 200 words."
You'll know it worked when Gemini replies with a readable summary that mentions real names and amounts from your statement — not a generic answer about budgeting.

## Step 4 — Ask about recurring charges and small fees
Now go one level deeper. Small monthly fees — a $4.99 streaming service, a $12 "account maintenance" charge, a $2 ATM surcharge — are easy to miss when you scroll quickly. Ask Gemini to look specifically for anything that appears more than once, or anything that looks like a fee rather than a purchase. This is the step where most people discover charges they've been paying for months without noticing. If Gemini says it can't see any recurring charges, the file may have been only partially read — ask it to look at every page, or paste the full transaction list into the chat.
💬 Example: "Now look only at the charges that happened more than once this month, and anything that looks like a fee or service charge. For each one, tell me the name, the amount, and how many times it appeared."
You'll know it worked when you get a short list of repeated merchants and fee names you can scan in 30 seconds — and probably one or two that surprise you.

## Step 5 — Ask about your real spending patterns
The next question is about categories. Gemini can group your transactions by type — food, transport, subscriptions, cash withdrawals — and show you where most of the money went. This is helpful even if your statement already has a "category" column, because Gemini's version often groups things more sensibly for everyday reading, and you can ask follow-up questions about any category that looks too big or too small. If Gemini lumps almost everything into "other," your statement may have lots of unfamiliar merchant names — ask it to list the biggest "other" items so you can see what got hidden.
💬 Example: "Group all my spending from this statement into simple categories like food, transport, subscriptions, bills and other. Show me the total for each category and the percentage of my total spending. Then tell me which category grew the most compared to a normal month."
You'll know it worked when you see a small table or list with named categories, dollar totals and clear percentages — something you could read once and remember.

## Step 6 — Save your insights or turn them into questions for your bank
The last step is making sure you don't lose what you just learned. If something in the summary or the fee list looked wrong, copy Gemini's exact wording of that charge — the merchant name, the date, the amount — and use it next time you contact your bank. You can also ask Gemini to rewrite the whole summary into an email or a checklist you can save. To come back to this conversation later, look in the left sidebar for your recent chats — your version of Gemini should keep a running list you can reopen. If you can't find it, bookmark the page in your browser before you close the tab.
💬 Example: "Turn the summary from Step 3 and the fee list from Step 4 into a short email I can send to my bank asking about the $12 monthly fee. Keep the tone polite and include the date and amount for each charge."
You'll know it worked when you have either a saved conversation, a copyable email draft, or a clear list of questions to bring to your bank's customer service.

## Common mistakes
- **Uploading a statement from a bank that masks real names.** Some banks replace merchant names with codes (like "POS DEBIT 8842"). Gemini can't decode those on its own — you'll get a vague answer. If this happens, ask your bank for an itemized version.
- **Asking one giant question instead of several small ones.** A request like "tell me everything about my statement" usually produces a fuzzy answer. Three or four short, focused questions (like in Steps 3, 4 and 5) get sharper results.
- **Forgetting to remove sensitive info if you share the chat.** A bank statement has your account number, sometimes your address and always your full name. If you ever screenshot a Gemini chat to share it, blur those parts first.
- **Treating Gemini's answer as a final verdict.** It can misread a number, miss a charge or guess wrong about a fee. Always check the original statement before calling your bank — Gemini helps you ask better questions, it doesn't replace them.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time a charge looks unfamiliar on your statement, you can paste it into Gemini and ask, in one sentence, "what is this $9.50 charge from XYZ?" before you spend 20 minutes on hold with customer service.
- **For your business or work:** if you run a small business and review statements monthly, this same set of questions can become a 5-minute weekly check instead of a 90-minute pile of receipts.
- **If you're just getting started:** try it on a statement you already understand well — your last month, perhaps. That way you can quickly see whether Gemini's summary is accurate, before you trust it on a more confusing one.

## Try it now
Open Gemini, upload this month's bank statement, and paste this single prompt: "Read this statement and list every charge I don't recognize, with the date and amount. Keep it to 10 items or fewer." Ninety seconds, one question — and you'll likely learn at least one thing you didn't know you were paying for.
